title: 504 Gateway Timeout
description: Fix requests that exceed proxy or PHP execution limits — common during imports, backups, or slow database queries.

steps.title: Identify Affected URLs or Actions
steps.instructions: Note which pages or admin actions timeout (imports, plugin updates, sitemap generation). Reproduce on staging with browser dev tools Network tab open.

steps.title: Increase Timeout and Execution Limits
steps.instructions: Raise max_execution_time and max_input_time in php.ini. Ask your host to increase nginx proxy_read_timeout or Apache Timeout if needed.

steps.title: Find Slow Database Queries
steps.instructions: Enable SAVEQUERIES or use Query Monitor on staging. Add missing indexes, clean postmeta/revisions, and disable plugins that run heavy queries on every request.

steps.title: Check External HTTP Calls
steps.instructions: Plugins calling slow third-party APIs during page load can cause timeouts. Identify blocking wp_remote_get/post calls and defer them to cron or async jobs.

steps.title: Run Heavy Jobs in Smaller Batches
steps.instructions: Split large imports, image regenerations, or search-replace into smaller chunks via WP-CLI or plugin batch settings instead of one long HTTP request.

steps.title: Add or Verify Object Caching
steps.instructions: Redis or Memcached reduces repeated DB hits. Confirm object cache is connected and not misconfigured (wrong host/port causes long connection waits).

steps.title: Retest Critical Paths
steps.instructions: Confirm previously timing-out URLs load within acceptable limits. Document new timeout values and any cron-based alternatives for heavy tasks.
